```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork)
library(wordcountaddin)
```

### Introduction

This report analyzes monthly McDonald's McFlurry machine status from November 2025 through October 2026 in the United States. Store-level analyses are combined with location and region information to explore brokenness, changes over time, and geographic patterns. Brokenness is analyzed only for observations marked active; missing status records are not included.

### Data Cleaning & Overview
```{r, warning = FALSE}

# Importing all monthly datasets
monthly_mcbroken <- list.files(
  path = "mcbroken_data",
  pattern = NULL,
  full.names = TRUE
  )

# Combining monthly datasets
mcbroken_raw <- map_dfr(monthly_mcbroken, read_csv)

# Widening date variable and changing variable types
mcbroken_clean <- mcbroken_raw %>%
  mutate(
    year = substr(month, 1, 4),
    month = substr(month, 6, 7),
    across(
      c(month, store_id, year),
           as.factor),
  )

# Importing store information datasets
store_info <- read_csv("store_data/store_info.csv")
state_regions <- read_csv("store_data/state_regions.csv")

# Matching variable types before joining
store_info <- store_info %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(store_id, state, city),
      as.factor)
    )

state_regions <- state_regions %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(state, region),
      as.factor)
    )

# Joining McBroken and store information datasets
mcbroken_clean <- mcbroken_clean %>%
  left_join(store_info, by = "store_id") %>%
  left_join(state_regions, by = "state")

# Store quantification
n_stores = n_distinct(mcbroken_clean$store_id)

state_store_counts <- mcbroken_clean %>% 
  count(state, sort = TRUE)

state_most_machines <- state_store_counts %>%
  slice_head(n=1)
state_most_machines

state_least_machines <- state_store_counts %>%
  slice_tail(n=1)
state_least_machines

# Overall brokenness rate among active machines
brokenness_rate_overall <- mcbroken_clean %>%
  summarise(
    status_number = sum(!is.na(active)),
    active_number = sum(active %in% TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    inactive_number = sum(active %in% FALSE, na.rm = TRUE),
    broken_number = sum(broken %in% TRUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    broken_rate_overall = 100*broken_number/active_number,
  )
```

To clean this data, I first imported and merged the monthly McFlurry machine status datasets and separated the date variable into month and year. After importing store information datasets and adjusting all variable types appropriately, I merged the McFlurry machine status and store information datasets into one dataframe. The resulting cleaned dataframe includes a total of `r nrow(mcbroken_clean)` observations across `r ncol(mcbroken_clean)` variables, including McFlurry machine status and brokenness, date, and store location information. 

There are data on McFlurry machines at `r n_stores` different McDonald's locations in the U.S., with California having the most stores at `r state_most_machines$n` and the Northern Mariana Islands having the least at `r state_least_machines$n`. The overall rate of brokenness of active McFlurry machines across all U.S. McDonald's locations between November 2025 and October 2026 was `r round(brokenness_rate_overall$broken_rate, 2)`%.
